suggestions.description: The dense catalog filter elides away the distinguishing part of actual tag names, preventing informed tag selection and identification of the included tag.

The case state and recorded real next-page selection check identify the included item as tag:Actual tag 16, state=1; this identity cannot be read from its selected control.

HANDOFF.md describes named three-state tags, and DESIGN_HANDOFF.md:406 requires ordering, publication states, and three-state tags; preserving actual data is not a waiver for losing visible filter identity.
suggestions.recommendation: Size tag controls from their real labels, reduce the number of columns or wrap labels, and recompute pagination so each tag retains a distinguishable name together with its include/exclude marker. Let short final pages use the available width.

suggestions.description: The category page does not explicitly identify creation and renaming as unavailable in this candidate.
evidence: The PNG shows the four real category counts and a gray disabled New category button, but no unavailable status and no visible rename capability state.
Case metadata records settings_details enabled=false for every category row, an empty settings_status, and the intentional difference that custom creation/rename is unavailable.

The current review instruction explicitly requires unavailable creation/rename to be clear. DESIGN_HANDOFF.md:578-579 requires concrete behavior or an honest unavailable state; HANDOFF.md lists category Rename and New category controls.

Gray styling is a valid disabled treatment under DESIGN_HANDOFF.md:102. This finding concerns the additional explicit capability state required by the task, not a claim of fake success or a requirement to implement custom categories in this round.
suggestions.recommendation: Add a concise unavailable status for category creation and renaming, and expose the corresponding disabled action state where appropriate. Use a short status label rather than explanatory prose, preserving real counts and avoiding any success simulation.

suggestions.description: Long English descriptions are paginated inside words, interrupting normal reading at page boundaries.
evidence: The first description page visibly ends 'An actual loopback p', exactly matching the end of its panel_text.
The supplied final description page begins 'rovider record used for native capture', exactly matching the beginning of its panel_text.
The full repeated phrase in these actual description records uses 'provider'; the screenshots therefore expose partial words rather than complete word-boundary pages. No text loss is asserted.
suggestions.recommendation: Choose description page boundaries at word or paragraph boundaries where possible while preserving every character, and continue allowing the final sheet height to follow its actual content.

limitations: This is a supplemental static review of eight supplied candidate states, not an exact pixel match against independent per-state reference PNGs or a complete clean-round verdict.
Only the eight input candidate PNGs were opened. No image scaling, recoloring, cropping, generated contact sheet, or alternative candidate/reference image was used.

Existing mechanical checks and action evidence were read as case identity/context; their passed flags were not treated as visual approval. No application, build, test, smoke check, or runtime probe was executed locally or remotely for this review.

Pagination controls are visible and metadata retains 34 tags, but the screenshots do not prove every later source/tag page, pointer target, outside-dismiss action, or persistence behavior. The two neutral tag captures do not visually establish the intermediate exclude state.

Real titles, source names, counts, time, unavailable update/size values, and saved configuration states may differ from prototype fixtures. These allowances do not waive tag readability, control access, or explicit unavailable capability states.

These cases contain no closed-reader image or hardware/authentication panel. They cannot establish artwork-only closed-reader behavior, absence of an invisible footer-cycle target, absent-hardware gating, tracking authorization, waveform quality, physical wake restoration, or a 512 MiB memory qualification.
